title: 🌱💧 Design ETo calculation
text: Let’s download daily meteorological data one station January 2000 March 2025 (station A001 started operating May 2000): resulting data frame includes temperature, solar radiation, wind speed, humidity, atmospheric pressure. keep article reproducible without depending INMET server, data downloaded call bundled package loaded :
code: df <- download_AWS_INMET_daily(   stations   = "A001",   start_date = "2000-01-01",   end_date   = "2025-03-31" ) df <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "A001_daily_2000_2025.rds", package = "BrazilMet")) df$date <- as.Date(df$date)

title: 🌱💧 Design ETo calculation
text: long series many sensor failures, missing input makes ETo NA day. fill_gaps() fills short gaps (three days) linear interpolation remaining ones mean day year years. Every filled value flagged *_filled column:

title: 🌧️ Sequential Water Balance (Thornthwaite-Mather)
text: article shows compute sequential soil water balance water_balance(), using real daily data INMET automatic weather station. workflow : Load daily weather data station. Fill short gaps left sensor failures fill_gaps(). Estimate reference evapotranspiration (ETo) FAO-56 Penman-Monteith. Run daily water balance given available water capacity (AWC, also known CAD). Aggregate results monthly balance compare different soil AWC values. function follows method Thornthwaite & Mather (1955). tracks accumulated potential water loss, soil water storage (arm), actual evapotranspiration (etr), water deficit (def) water excess (exc). time step defined resolution input vectors, function works daily, weekly monthly balances.

title: 🌧️ Sequential Water Balance (Thornthwaite-Mather)
text: Automatic stations occasional sensor failures, functions follow need complete series. Count missing values variables used compute ETo: fill_gaps() fills isolated gaps linear interpolation. gaps max_gap days filled, long outages never invented, *_filled column flags every filled value. Rainfall deliberately filled: intermittent, interpolation create rain occur (missing rainfall values series).
code: eto_vars <- c("tair_mean_c", "tair_min_c", "tair_max_c", "rh_max_porc",               "rh_min_porc", "ws_2_m_s", "patm_mb", "sr_mj_m2")  colSums(is.na(df[eto_vars])) #> tair_mean_c  tair_min_c  tair_max_c rh_max_porc rh_min_porc    ws_2_m_s  #>          29          29          29          30          30          33  #>     patm_mb    sr_mj_m2  #>          28           7 df <- fill_gaps(df, vars = eto_vars, max_gap = 3) #> Filled values (remaining NA): tair_mean_c = 29 (0), tair_min_c = 29 (0), tair_max_c = 29 (0), rh_max_porc = 30 (0), rh_min_porc = 30 (0), ws_2_m_s = 33 (0), patm_mb = 28 (0), sr_mj_m2 = 7 (0)  colSums(is.na(df[eto_vars])) #> tair_mean_c  tair_min_c  tair_max_c rh_max_porc rh_min_porc    ws_2_m_s  #>           0           0           0           0           0           0  #>     patm_mb    sr_mj_m2  #>           0           0

ETo calculated with FAO-56 Penman-Monteith."   ) +   theme_bm()

text: storage percentage AWC shows soil full, dries fast replenished:
code: ggplot(bal_daily, aes(x = period, y = awc_arm)) +   geom_area(fill = col_storage, alpha = 0.25) +   geom_line(colour = col_storage, linewidth = 0.7) +   geom_hline(yintercept = 50, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +   scale_x_date(date_breaks = "3 months", date_labels = "%b\n%Y", expand = c(0, 0)) +   scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100), labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")) +   labs(     title    = "Soil water storage",     subtitle = "Percentage of the available water capacity (AWC = 100 mm)",     x        = NULL,     y        = "Soil water storage (% of AWC)",     caption  = "Dashed line: 50% of AWC."   ) +   theme_bm()

title: 🌧️ Sequential Water Balance (Thornthwaite-Mather)
text: function can applied time step. , daily rainfall ETo summed month balance recalculated time_step = "monthly": classic extended water balance chart displays monthly water excess (zero) water deficit (zero):
code: df$month <- as.Date(format(df$date, "%Y-%m-01"))  monthly <- aggregate(cbind(rainfall_mm, eto) ~ month, data = df, FUN = sum)  bal_monthly <- water_balance(   ppt       = monthly$rainfall_mm,   etp       = monthly$eto,   AWC       = 100,   period    = monthly$month,   time_step = "monthly" )  head(round(bal_monthly[, c("ppt", "etp", "arm", "etr", "def", "exc")], 1), 6) #>     ppt   etp arm   etr  def exc #> 1 190.8 136.5 100 136.5  0.0  54 #> 2  55.0 140.7  42 113.0 27.7   0 #> 3 135.2 129.2  48 129.2  0.0   0 #> 4 187.6 108.8 100 108.8  0.0  27 #> 5   1.4 118.4  31  70.0 48.4   0 #> 6   2.2 108.4  11  22.0 86.4   0 ggplot(bal_monthly, aes(x = period)) +   geom_col(aes(y = exc, fill = "Excess"), width = 25) +   geom_col(aes(y = -def, fill = "Deficit"), width = 25) +   geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey30") +   scale_fill_manual(values = c("Excess" = col_excess, "Deficit" = col_deficit)) +   scale_x_date(date_breaks = "2 months", date_labels = "%b\n%Y") +   labs(     title    = "Monthly water excess and deficit",     subtitle = "Thornthwaite-Mather balance, AWC = 100 mm",     x        = NULL,     y        = "mm / month",     caption  = "Source: INMET station A001."   ) +   theme_bm()

title: 🌧️ Sequential Water Balance (Thornthwaite-Mather)
text: Annual water balance components (mm)
code: bal_monthly$year <- format(bal_monthly$period, "%Y")  annual <- aggregate(cbind(ppt, etp, etr, def, exc) ~ year, data = bal_monthly, FUN = sum) names(annual) <- c("Year", "Rainfall", "ETo", "ETR", "Deficit", "Excess")  knitr::kable(annual, digits = 0, caption = "Annual water balance components (mm)")

title: 🌧️ Sequential Water Balance (Thornthwaite-Mather)
text: AWC controls much water soil can store, main parameter adapt balance given crop soil. daily balance run three AWC values:  Total water deficit period, AWC
code: awc_values <- c(50, 100, 150)  bal_awc <- do.call(rbind, lapply(awc_values, function(awc) {   b <- water_balance(     ppt       = df$rainfall_mm,     etp       = df$eto,     AWC       = awc,     period    = df$date,     time_step = "daily"   )   b$AWC <- factor(paste("AWC =", awc, "mm"), levels = paste("AWC =", awc_values, "mm"))   b })) ggplot(bal_awc, aes(x = period, y = awc_arm, colour = AWC)) +   geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +   scale_colour_manual(values = c("#E69F00", "#0072B2", "#009E73")) +   scale_x_date(date_breaks = "3 months", date_labels = "%b\n%Y", expand = c(0, 0)) +   scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100), labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")) +   labs(     title    = "Soil water storage for different AWC values",     subtitle = "Soils with lower AWC dry out faster at the start of the dry season",     x        = NULL,     y        = "Soil water storage (% of AWC)",     caption  = "Source: INMET station A001."   ) +   theme_bm() total_deficit <- aggregate(def ~ AWC, data = bal_awc, FUN = sum) names(total_deficit) <- c("Soil", "Total deficit (mm)")  knitr::kable(total_deficit, caption = "Total water deficit in the period, by AWC")

what: Fill gaps in daily weather data — fill_gaps
title: Fill gaps in daily weather data — fill_gaps
text: Fills missing values (`NA`) daily weather variables, data downloaded [download_AWS_INMET_daily()], can used functions accept missing values, like [water_balance()]. Short gaps filled linear interpolation neighbouring observations, , optionally, remaining gaps filled mean day year across available years (climatology). Precipitation must filled function: intermittent, interpolation averaging create rainfall occur. column flags (`<variable>_filled`) identifies every value filled, filled data never mistaken observations.

title: Fill gaps in daily weather data — fill_gaps
code: fill_gaps(   data,   vars = c("tair_mean_c", "tair_min_c", "tair_max_c", "rh_max_porc", "rh_min_porc",     "ws_2_m_s", "patm_mb", "sr_mj_m2"),   date = "date",   method = c("linear", "climatology", "both"),   max_gap = 3,   group = NULL,   flag = TRUE )

title: Fill gaps in daily weather data — fill_gaps
text: data data.frame one row per day. vars character vector names columns fill. default set INMET variables used [daily_eto_FAO56()]. Rainfall columns allowed. date Name column dates (`Date` `POSIXct`). Within group, dates must unique sorted ascending order. method `"linear"` (default) interpolates gaps `max_gap` days two observed values; short gaps beginning end series take nearest observation. `"climatology"` fills every gap mean day year years (needs one year data). `""` applies linear interpolation first climatology remains. max_gap Maximum length, days, gap filled linear interpolation. Longer gaps left `NA` (filled climatology `method = ""`). Default 3. group Optional name column (e.g. station code) used fill series independently data one station. flag `TRUE` (default), adds logical column `<variable>_filled` filled variable.

title: Fill gaps in daily weather data — fill_gaps
text: input data.frame missing values filled ,   `flag = TRUE`, one extra `<variable>_filled` column per variable.   message reports many values filled many remain missing.

title: Fill gaps in daily weather data — fill_gaps
text: Roberto Filgueiras

Sequential water balance (Thornthwaite-Mather) — water_balance
text: Calculates soil water balance using precipitation potential evapotranspiration sequence periods, following Thornthwaite & Mather (1955) method. time step balance (daily, weekly, monthly custom interval) entirely defined resolution `ppt` `etp`: recursive logic (accumulated potential water loss, soil water storage, actual evapotranspiration, deficit, excess) regardless period length, daily PPT/ETP produce daily balance, weekly sums produce weekly balance, . available water capacity soil (AWC, also known CAD) can freely adjusted match crop/soil modeled.

title: Sequential water balance (Thornthwaite-Mather) — water_balance
code: water_balance(   ppt,   etp,   AWC,   period = NULL,   year = NULL,   group = NULL,   time_step = c("daily", "weekly", "monthly", "custom") )

title: Sequential water balance (Thornthwaite-Mather) — water_balance
text: ppt numeric vector precipitation (irrigation + precipitation) period, units `etp`. etp numeric vector potential (reference) evapotranspiration period, length `ppt`. AWC single positive numeric value available water capacity (CAD) soil, depth units `ppt`/`etp` (e.g. mm). Can set value required soil/crop simulated. period Optional vector identifying period (e.g. dates, day year, week number, month number), length `ppt`. Used label output; affect calculation. year Optional vector identifying year associated period, length `ppt`. Used label output. group Optional vector (e.g. station ID site name), length `ppt`, used run independent balances different series stacked input (group restarts recursion assuming soil starts field capacity). Rows group must contiguous already ordered time. `NULL` (default), single continuous balance calculated whole input. time_step label indicating time step represented row: `"daily"`, `"weekly"`, `"monthly"` `"custom"`. stored reference/documentation purposes change calculation.

title: Sequential water balance (Thornthwaite-Mather) — water_balance
text: data.frame (optional) `group`, `year` `period`   columns, inputs `ppt` `etp`, `time_step` used,   calculated columns: `ppt_etp` (P - ETP), `neg_ac` (accumulated potential   water loss, "negativo acumulado"), `arm` (soil water storage), `alt`   (change storage), `etr` (actual evapotranspiration), `def` (water   deficit), `exc` (water excess), `awc_arm` (percentage AWC stored).
